title: Farrukhsiyar’s Warning Against Opposing the House of Nanak

blocks.text: Farrukhsiyar first resists the anti-Sikh pressure placed before him. He repeats my grandfather’s advice that the court must not oppose the House of Nanak and recalls that the Guru’s blessing had once strengthened Mughal sovereignty rather than threatened it.
That restraint does not end the intrigue. The backbiters returned almost immediately, insisting that Banda was oppressing the country and reaching for rule over all Hindustan.

The page therefore marks a brief pause before renewed hostility. Its key movement is the emperor’s warning not to oppose the House of Nanak, followed by the courtly agitation that pushes him back toward war.
